source.title: Some Open Problems Related to Creative Telescoping

accepted.question_text: Develop a reduction-based creative telescoping algorithm for a hypergeometric-hyperexponential term f_n(x) in the summation setting. The algorithm should compute, when possible, rational functions c_0(x), c_1(x), ..., c_r(x) in C(x), not all zero, together with a hypergeometric-hyperexponential term g_n(x), such that c_0 f_n(x) + c_1 D_x f_n(x) + ... + c_r D_x^r f_n(x) = g_{n+1}(x) - g_n(x).
accepted.context_brief: Reduction-based creative telescoping for mixed terms

evidence.quote: Problem 2.1 Develop a reduction based creative telescoping algorithm which for a given hypergeometric-hyperexponential term fn(x) computes, if possible, rational functions c0, c1, ··· , cr in C(x), not all zero, such that there exists a hypergeometric-hyperexponential term gn(x) with c0fn(x) + c1Dxfn(x) + ··· + crDr_xfn(x) = gn+1(x) − gn(x).

accepted.question_text: Develop a reduction-based creative telescoping algorithm for a given Fuchsian D-finite function f(x, y). The algorithm should compute, when possible, rational functions c_0(x), c_1(x), ..., c_r(x) in C(x), not all zero, and an operator Q in C(x, y)[D_x, D_y] such that (c_0 + c_1 D_x + ... + c_r D_x^r) · f = D_y Q · f.
accepted.context_brief: Reduction-based creative telescoping for D-finite functions

evidence.quote: Problem 2.2 Develop a reduction based creative telescoping algorithm which for a given (Fuchsian) D-finite function f(x, y) computes, if possible, rational functions c0, c1, ··· , cr ∈ C(x), not all zero, such that there exists an operator Q ∈ C(x, y)[Dx, Dy] with (c0 + c1Dx + ··· + crDr_x) · f = DyQ · f.

accepted.question_text: Derive an order-degree curve for general D-finite functions, meaning a bound that describes how the degree of a telescoper can depend on a chosen operator order for telescopers of those functions.

evidence.quote: Problem 3.1 Derive an order-degree-curve for general D-finite functions.

accepted.question_text: Derive bounds for the bit size of telescopers for hyperexponential terms.

evidence.quote: Problem 3.2 Derive bounds for the bit size of telescopers for hyperexponential terms.

accepted.question_text: Given a proper hypergeometric term f(n, k) = p c^n d^k ∏_{i=1}^m Γ(α_i n + β_i k + γ_i)^{e_i}, where p ∈ C[n, k], c and d are in C, α_i, β_i, e_i are in N, and γ_i are in C, find a method to determine the removable and non-removable singularities of a telescoper for f using less computation than is required to compute a telescoper itself. Ask the analogous question for hyperexponential terms f(x, y) = exp(a/b) ∏_{i=1}^m p_i^{c_i}, where a, b, p_i ∈ C[x, y] and c_i ∈ C.

evidence.quote: Problem 3.3 (a) Find a way to determine the removable and non-removable singularities of a telescoper for a given proper hypergeometric term f(n, k) = pcndk ∏_{i=1}^m Γ(αin+βik+γi)^{ei} (p ∈ C[n, k], c, d ∈ C, αi, βi, ei ∈ N, γi ∈ C), using less computation time than needed for computing a telescoper. (b) The analogous question for hyperexponential terms f(x, y)= exp(a/b) ∏_{i=1}^m p_i^{c_i} (a, b, p_i ∈ C[x, y], c_i ∈ C).

accepted.question_text: For creative telescoping over liouvillean fields in the differential setting, and over ΠΣ-fields in the shift setting, derive a criterion that decides when a telescoper exists. In every case where telescopers do exist, also derive bounds on their order.
accepted.context_brief: Existence and order of telescopers over fields

evidence.quote: Problem 4.1 For the creative telescoping problem over liouvillean fields (in the differential case) or for ΠΣ-fields (in the shift case), derive a criterion for the existence of a telescoper. For the cases where telescopers exist, derive bounds on their order.

accepted.question_text: Design an algorithm that takes an expression built from nested indefinite integrals and returns an equivalent expression whose nesting depth is as small as possible.
accepted.context_brief: Minimizing nesting depth of indefinite integrals

evidence.quote: Problem 4.2 Design an algorithm which finds for a given expression of nested indefinite integrals an equivalent expression for which the the nesting depth is as small as possible.

accepted.question_text: Determine the class of elementary functions f with the property that, for every natural number n, the n-fold integral of f is again an elementary function.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.3 Determine the class of elementary functions with the property that for every n ∈ N, their n-fold integral is again elementary.

accepted.question_text: Develop an algorithm that takes as input a multivariate hypergeometric term h in discrete variables k_1, k_2, ..., k_m and decides whether there exist hypergeometric terms g_1, g_2, ..., g_m such that h = Δ_1(g_1) + Δ_2(g_2) + ... + Δ_m(g_m), where Δ_i is the forward difference operator in k_i defined by Δ_i f(k_1, ..., k_i, ..., k_m) = f(k_1, ..., k_i + 1, ..., k_m) - f(k_1, ..., k_i, ..., k_m).

evidence.quote: Problem 5.1 Develop an algorithm which takes as input a multivariate hypergeometric term h in m discrete variables k1, k2, ··· , km, and decides whether there exist hypergeometric terms g1, g2, ··· , gm such that h = Δ1(g1)+Δ2(g2) + ··· + Δm(gm). Here, Δi is the forward difference operator with respect to the variable ki.

accepted.question_text: Develop an algorithm that starts from a telescoper-certificate relation for a hypergeometric term and correctly turns it into a recurrence for the associated definite sum, while properly handling all issues caused by poles in the certificate.

evidence.quote: Problem 6.1 Develop an algorithm that correctly transforms a telescoper-certificate pair for a hypergeometric term into a recurrence for the corresponding definite sum. In particular, the algorithm should properly take care of any possible issues arising from poles in the certificate.

accepted.question_text: Develop a theory of operator algebras that contains both shift operators and summation operators, analogous to the integro-differential operator algebras of Regensburger and Rosenkranz. Within that theory, explain algebraically why the right-hand side of a creative telescoping relation often vanishes for binomial sums.
accepted.context_brief: Operator algebras with shifts and summation

evidence.quote: Problem 6.2 Develop a theory of operator algebras including shift as well as summation operators, analogous to the theory of Regensburger and Rosenkranz. In this theory, find an algebraic explanation why the right hand side of a creative telescoping relation often vanishes for binomial sums.

accepted.question_text: Develop a creative telescoping algorithm for functions that satisfy systems of algebraic differential equations. Here the source motivates the class by examples such as exp(y(e^x − 1)), the partition generating function ∏_{n=0}^∞ (1 − x^n)^{-1}, and the Weierstrass ℘-function, all of which satisfy algebraic differential equations but are not necessarily D-finite.

evidence.quote: Problem 7.2 Develop a creative telescoping algorithm applicable to functions satisfying systems of ADEs.

accepted.question_text: Design an algorithm that takes as input a nonzero recurrence operator P ∈ Q[n][S_n] and, when possible, finds a bivariate hypergeometric term f(n, k) for which P is a telescoper, meaning that there exists a certificate operator Q with P − (S_k − 1)Q annihilating f.

evidence.quote: Problem 8.1 Design an algorithm which takes as input a nonzero recurrence operator P ∈ Q[n][Sn] and finds, if at all possible, a bivariate hypergeometric term f(n, k) which has P as a telescoper.

accepted.question_text: For each d in {4, 5, ..., 12}, prove recurrence equations for the diagonal coefficient sequence of the rational series 1 / (1 − Σ_{i=1}^d x_i/(1 − x_i)). Here the diagonal means the univariate series obtained by taking coefficients a_{n,n,...,n} from the underlying d-variate power series.
accepted.context_brief: Recurrences for diagonals of rational series

evidence.quote: Problem 9.1 For d = 4, 5, ··· , 12, prove recurrence equations for the diagonals of the rational series 1/(1 − ∑_{i=1}^d x_i/(1−x_i)) conjectured in [104].

accepted.question_text: For n = 10, 11, and 12, compute the Ehrhart polynomial H_n(t) defined by the contour integral H_n(t) = (1/(2πi)^n) ∮_{|z_1|=ε_1} ... ∮_{|z_n|=ε_n} (z_1 z_2 ... z_n)^(−t−1) (∏_{k=1}^n z_k^{t+n−1} / ∏_{j=k+1}^n (z_k − z_j))^n dz_n ... dz_2 dz_1, where 0 < ε_1, ε_2, ..., ε_n < 1 are arbitrary. The challenge is to compute the polynomial itself, not merely a differential equation that it satisfies.

evidence.quote: Problem 9.2 For n = 10, 11, 12, compute the polynomial Hn(t) = 1/(2πi)^n ∮_{|z1|=ε1} ∮_{|z2|=ε2} ··· ∮_{|zn|=εn} (z1z2 ··· zn)^{−t−1} (∏_{k=1}^n z_k^{t+n−1} / ∏_{j=k+1}^n (zk − zj))^n dzn ··· dz2dz1, where 0 < ε1, ε2, ··· , εn < 1 are arbitrary.
